arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The government argues the defendant received adequate advice about counsel rights. It claims he pleaded guilty with counsel present and after prior warnings.
The defendant argues the court failed to explain counsel's specific role in trial. It claims the court did not link counsel to confronting witnesses.
The government emphasizes the finality of carefully taken guilty pleas. It argues courts should not lightly set aside valid pleas.
The defendant highlights the need for clear explanations of legal rights. It argues vague advice fails to protect defendants' constitutional rights.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the minimum advice required for a valid guilty plea. It determines whether courts must explain how counsel affects trial rights. It protects defendants from unknowingly waiving critical legal protections during plea negotiations.
